_strings.@@fa16435bb1c5: Treaty conformity — AZ conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from AZ income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the AZ return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Arizona's resident return (Form 140) starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2024 Form 140 line 12 is "Federal adjusted gross income (from your federal return)", and the 2024 instructions state "Arizona uses federal adjusted gross income as a starting point to determine Arizona taxable income. Your federal adjusted gross income is your Arizona gross income." Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to the AZ return excluded. AZ then applies only specific statutory additions (2024 Form 140 lines 14-18): the small-business-income modification (lines 13-14), non-Arizona municipal bond interest (line 15), the Form 165 Schedule K-1 partnership income adjustment (line 16), total federal depreciation (line 17, reversed via the line 26 subtraction), and line 18 "Other Additions to Arizona Gross Income" (the 2024 instructions enumerate items A-J: married-filing-separate community-income splits, fiduciary adjustments, the ordinary-income portion of federally-averaged lump-sum distributions, items previously deducted for Arizona purposes, claim-of-right repayments, and sole-proprietorship items such as Arizona marijuana businesses and nonprofit medical marijuana dispensaries). No line on Form 140 or its additions schedule adds back federal tax-treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA). Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by Arizona -> conforms. (The full 2024 additions instructions were read from the fetched 140i PDF — an improvement over the 2023 pack, which relied on search snippets.)

Pack notes: Rate unchanged for 2024: Arizona stays at the 2.5% flat rate for all income levels and filing statuses (first effective 2023); the standard deduction rose to the printed 2024 federal amounts ($14,600/$29,200/$21,900, from $13,850/$27,700/$20,800), and the lines 38-41 exemption amounts are unchanged. Arizona has NO personal exemption, and the plain dependent exemption was replaced by the Line 49 Dependent Tax Credit ($100 per dependent under 17, $25 per dependent 17 or over, phased down when federal AGI exceeds $200,000 — $400,000 MFJ, no credit once the excess tops $19,000). It is a CREDIT against tax, not a base reduction, and is NOT modeled by calc.state_tax. The 2024 Arizona standard deduction equals the printed 2024 federal amounts. Increased Standard Deduction for charitable contributions (Line 44): non-itemizers may add 33% (.33) of qualified charitable contributions (2024 rate, up from 31% in 2023) via the Form 140 page-3 worksheet — NOT modeled; claim it on Line 44 with box 44C checked. Exemptions on Form 140 lines 38-41 (age 65+ $2,100; blind $1,500; other $2,300; qualifying parent/grandparent $10,000) reduce Arizona AGI on the form — calc.state_tax does not apply them; a 65+/blind filer computes lines 38-41 on the form.
